source: Nine Years. We Kept The Receipts. (17 Nov 2026 plan); numbers from monthly_targets, monthly_plans and the April 2027 offers in p57-data/studio.db
title: Nine Years. We Kept The Receipts.
subtitle: Physique 57 India · April 2027 · one mechanic, seven offers, five things to run and nothing to procure but keys and a printer
summary: April 2027 target: ₹119.6L across the four locations, against ₹90.7L in April 2026. Seven offers carry ₹103.5L of it (87%); the rest is full-price trade. Nine years of a studio means nine years of a file on every person who walked in — classes taken, classes skipped, longest streak, longest disappearance. The studio doesn't joke about you. It just reads your record back to you, on receipt paper, with the April offer printed at the bottom. No offer above 25% effective; renewal and early renewal held at 15–18% value-back so there is discount left to pull if week three is soft.
idea: Nine years. Every rep logged. Every excuse filed. One mechanic at every location for every segment: a thermal printer at each front desk prints anyone's record — on file since, classes taken, longest streak, longest silence — and the month's offer prints underneath. It's savage in the only way that lands, which is specific and true: "Booked 41 classes. Attended 24." is a joke the client wrote themselves over nine years. People photograph it, which is free reach, and nobody has to be handed a prop for it to work. The status line is the collectible; clients will compare them, which is the point. Voice rules: flat declaratives, no exclamation marks, never explain the joke. The studio is not excited for you — it is a bureaucrat with a grudge and a nine-year memory. Nothing in the copy says "celebrate", "journey" or "family".

why.head: One idea, repeatable in a sentence
why.body: They printed my whole history and it was brutal. That is the only test a theme has to pass: something a client can repeat to a friend. The old draft had five unrelated jokes — death, a casino, a lease signing, a panic attack, a fortune cookie.

why.head: The studio has standing
why.body: Most boutique studios in this city don't see nine years. Smugness is earned, so the brand gets to be insufferable on purpose.

why.head: It personalises at scale without staffing
why.body: A séance can't scale to hundreds of new buyers, renewers and win-backs; a print job can. Momence holds the data, n8n builds the receipt, respond.io delivers the lapsed version.

why.head: It costs a thermal printer per studio
why.body: Roughly ₹4,000 each; four studios plus spare rolls lands under ₹20,000 for the month — against an arcade claw machine per studio, giant custom fortune cookies, a postcard print run and a built photo booth.

why.head: It covers the Pop-up
why.body: A Pop-up client's receipt is short and that's the joke: "On file since Feb. Classes: 6. Still calling it 'that pilates thing'." The Pop-up finally runs inside the anniversary instead of beside it.

why.head: The renewal math is arithmetic, not ambition
why.body: Every location needs more renewals in April than it has memberships expiring in April. Roughly half the renewal line has to be pulled forward from May–July or it doesn't exist — that is why Your Future Self Is Unreliable is in the plan.

offers.name: Suspiciously Clean Record
offers.headline: Nine years of records and not one of them has your name on it.
offers.details: The receipt prints NO RECORD FOUND and the offer underneath. Buy the 3-Month Unlimited within 9 hours of the first class: ₹47,441 in Mumbai, ₹34,612 at Kenkere (Pop-up: the 10-class pack at ₹7,229). The record is opened in front of them — the desk stamps the receipt ACCOUNT OPENED, it goes on the board, that's the photo. No confetti cannon, no fortune cookie, nothing to source.
offers.message: NO RECORD FOUND. Nine years of records and not one of them has your name on it. Fix that within 9 hours of your first class and the 3-Month is ₹47,441.
offers.job: Bring April's traffic in and convert it on the day the body feels best.
offers.why: The 9-hour window is the strongest mechanic in the slot: it buys on the day the body feels best and makes the price obviously a one-day price rather than the price.
offers.audience: First-time clients, within 9 hours of their first class.
offers.rules: One per phone number. 18% effective. Newcomers get a three-line receipt and a clean slate — no skip counts.
offers.kpi: Pass → member conversion; ACCOUNT OPENED stamps on the board.

offers.name: Last Seen Wearing Leggings
offers.headline: Last seen 14 August. Muttering about next week.
offers.details: Replaces the obituary postcards and the séance — not because the joke is too dark, but because of who it lands on: people lapse for injury, pregnancy, illness and bereavement, and a mock obituary posted to the wrong person is a brand problem you cannot apologise your way out of. Instead: a personalised respond.io message with their own record as an image — last class date, days elapsed, their old regular slot, their best streak. Missing-persons voice, no death. Then the 3-Month at ₹47,441 Mumbai / ₹35,034 Kenkere, plus one private to rebuild form.
offers.message: MISSING. Last seen 14 August, 7am Signature, third barre from the window. Reward offered: 3 months at ₹47,441 and a private to rebuild form.
offers.job: Win back the lapsed list with something more personal than anything you could have posted.
offers.why: Zero print run, zero staffing, and their own record is funnier and kinder than a joke a marketing team wrote. Suppression list applied before anything sends.
offers.audience: Clients lapsed 60+ days; suppression list applied first.
offers.rules: Full 25% kept for this slot. Lapsed clients get the dates, never the skip count.
offers.kpi: Record cards → returns; reactivations vs April 2026.

offers.name: Certified Insufferable
offers.headline: You've earned the smugness. Here's the paperwork.
offers.details: Structurally the best offer in the month and it stays: renew or upgrade at list price — ₹57,855 Mumbai / ₹42,210 Kenkere — with no percentage off. The reward scales to the receipt, not a machine: classes in the last 12 months decide the tier. Up to 30: 2 bonus classes + 7 days. 31–75: 3 bonus classes + 7 days + 1 virtual private. 76–150: adds 1 private + 2 freezes. 150+: all of it plus the hoodie, and the receipt prints in gold. The dare card stays, renamed Settle Your Account: keep the reward, double it by completing a dare (9 classes in 14 days; a 7am every week of May), or donate it as guest passes.
offers.message: CERTIFIED INSUFFERABLE. You've earned the smugness; here's the paperwork. Renew at list price and the receipt decides your reward.
offers.job: Protect the price in the month when the most people are buying.
offers.why: The tier is a lookup, not a machine you have to buy, fill, maintain and find floor space for in four studios. Extras cost less than face value, so value-back is held at 15–18%, leaving discount to pull if week three is soft. The dare card buys May attendance with April's money.
offers.audience: Members renewing or upgrading in April.
offers.rules: List price only. Value-back 15–18%. Reward tier read off classes in the last 12 months.
offers.kpi: April renewal yield vs April 2026; Settle Your Account dares completed.

offers.name: Your Future Self Is Unreliable
offers.headline: Your membership ends in June. You, historically, do not.
offers.details: Not optional — arithmetic. Every location needs more renewals in April than it has memberships expiring in April, so roughly half the renewal line has to be pulled forward from May–July or it doesn't exist. Anyone whose membership expires May, June or July renews during April at list price, gets the full Certified Insufferable value-back plus 9 bonus days on the back of their current term. No discount — the incentive is access to anniversary terms early, and nine days.
offers.message: Your membership ends in June. You, historically, do not. Renew it during April at list price and take the anniversary terms early, plus 9 bonus days on the end of your current term.
offers.job: Move May–July renewal revenue into the month that needs it.
offers.why: Costs nothing, and it's a clean WhatsApp campaign off a Momence expiry query. Kenkere's line is blended at the 1-Month renewal price because most of its expiries are short plans.
offers.audience: Members whose membership expires May, June or July.
offers.rules: List price only; value-back 15–18% plus 9 bonus days. The list goes out the morning of 5 April.
offers.kpi: May–July expiries renewed in April vs the pull-forward needed per studio.

offers.name: Nine Month Sentence
offers.headline: Nine months. No parole. Good behaviour earns freezes.
offers.details: The 9-Month Unlimited with the numbered keys is the best mechanic in the draft — real scarcity, a rising price, nothing to buy but keys and a counter — kept whole and renamed to fix the copy. Mumbai, 99 keys: ₹1,34,999 for 001–033, ₹1,39,999 for 034–066, ₹1,44,999 for 067–099, with a step at midnight on the 18th. 9 freezes (good behaviour earns them), the key is your release date, your name on the Lease Wall, a live counter on the studio screens. Platinum holders from 30 March. Now runs at Bandra and Kenkere too — the upsell slot no longer sits at ₹0 outside Kemps. Kenkere tiers ₹98,999 / ₹1,01,999 / ₹1,04,999 are inferred from the Mumbai ratio: confirm the Bengaluru 6-Month list price before this goes out.
offers.message: Nine months. No parole. Good behaviour earns freezes, and the key is your release date. 99 numbered keys in Mumbai; the rent goes up every 33 keys and again at midnight on the 18th.
offers.job: The biggest ticket of the month, carrying members to January 2028.
offers.why: A numbered, one-month-only product gives people a reason to buy now without cutting the price of the core memberships.
offers.audience: Members and returning clients ready for a long commitment; 99 numbered keys per city.
offers.rules: 22.9% effective at the lowest key price. No second batch, no price cut. April only.
offers.kpi: Keys sold vs the plan per studio; 6M+ share of April membership revenue.

offers.name: Plank Or Pay
offers.headline: Hold the plank, drop the price. Or wait for 9:09 and panic with everyone else.
offers.details: The Limited Edition 9-Class Pack, 99 days validity, all April. Hold a plank at the desk and the price drops: 57 seconds ₹12,999, 1:57 ₹12,249, 2:57 ₹11,499 — Kenkere ₹8,699 / ₹8,199 / ₹7,699. On 9 April, two 99-minute windows from 9:09am and 9:09pm, everyone gets the floor price with no plank, siren in studio, countdown on Instagram. The Pop-up runs it on the 10-class pack at ₹7,229 with the same plank ladder scaled down — which finally puts the Pop-up inside the anniversary instead of beside it.
offers.message: Plank for your price: 57 seconds is ₹12,999, 2:57 is ₹11,499. Or wait for 9:09 on 9 April, when everyone gets the floor price for 99 minutes. Panic responsibly.
offers.job: The anniversary's entry product and the loudest day of the month — entirely free to run.
offers.why: A price you earn with your body is the most Physique 57 thing there is, and every plank at the desk is a show for whoever is waiting. Plan revenue is counted at the floor.
offers.audience: Everyone: members, pack buyers and newcomers.
offers.rules: Spot offer, ≤25% effective at the floor. Two packs per person. No anniversary prices after 30 April.
offers.kpi: Packs sold in the two 9:09 windows; pack → membership by June.

offers.name: Prove It
offers.headline: For nine years you've told her she'd love this. Bring her.
offers.details: Nine years, four locations, and the old draft had no referral offer. A member brings someone with no record on file. The guest's first class is free, the guest unlocks Suspiciously Clean Record, and if they buy anything in April the member gets 2 bonus classes and 7 days. Cap 3 per member. The receipt handles the pitch: the member's own record prints with one line at the bottom — REFERRALS ON FILE: 0. For nine years. Interesting.
offers.message: REFERRALS ON FILE: 0. For nine years. Interesting. Bring her: her first class is free, and if she buys anything in April you get 2 bonus classes and 7 days.
offers.job: The cheapest new-client revenue available and the only lever that doesn't erode price.
offers.why: Most needed where growth is steepest — Kenkere at +65% and the Pop-up at +183%. The member reward is acquisition cost, paid only on a purchase.
offers.audience: Current members bringing a guest with no record on file.
offers.rules: Guest must be new to P57. Cap 3 per member. Guest buys at the Suspiciously Clean Record price.
offers.kpi: Referred buyers per studio; members reaching the cap of three.

risks.risk: The receipt tone lands wrong on the wrong client
risks.mitigation: The 100-class guardrail on skip counts; newcomers get a three-line receipt and a clean slate; lapsed clients get dates, never the skip count; everything tested on staff records first.

risks.risk: The win-back reaches someone it shouldn't
risks.mitigation: Saachi flags injury, pregnancy, medical and bereavement in Momence before anything sends. Missing-persons voice, no death, no obituary.

risks.risk: Kenkere's +65% doesn't live in any offer
risks.mitigation: Its binding constraint is lead→trial follow-up speed on leads that already exist — worth more than the whole offer set. Pull the follow-up timings and fix the leak; the offers are the floor, not the plan.

risks.risk: Everything priced at the ceiling leaves nothing for week three
risks.mitigation: Renewal and early renewal held at 15–18% value-back; the full 25% reserved for the flash day and the win-back; the mid-month read (19–25 Apr) decides if it gets spent.

risks.risk: No paid support where growth is steepest
risks.mitigation: offerRunAds is off on every row. Make it a deliberate decision, not a default — if it stays no, Kenkere's +65% needs a different source.

risks.risk: The receipt engine has no owner
risks.mitigation: It's a Momence query, an n8n flow and a print template — the new systems hire's first shipped project. If it's not him, it's Jimmy, and that changes what else April can carry.

Skip counts (booked-not-attended, late cancels) print only for clients with 100+ classes. Newcomers get three lines and a clean slate; lapsed clients get the dates, never the skip count.
Voice: flat declaratives, no exclamation marks, never explain the joke. Nothing says "celebrate", "journey" or "family".
Scarcity is real: 99 keys means 99 keys. No second batch, no price cut, no anniversary prices after 30 April.
